messages: image has empty alternative text and is not marked decorative
rules.change: accessibility extension; severity warning, where the 0.1 source sets error
rules.reports: an image that is neither decorative nor carries alt text, once per image: its alt is empty, as `![](a.png)`, or unknown (C2-A-115 names the three states); an image with alt text or `decorative: true` is not reported; a parse of Carve source never marks an image decorative and never leaves its alt unknown, so in source the rule reports exactly the empty alt (C2-I-074, C2-A-115)

messages: This bare HTML tag is escaped as text; use a raw HTML block if markup is intended.
rules.reports: the first HTML tag shape on a line of a paragraph, a heading or a pipe table row: `<`, an optional `/`, an ASCII letter, then ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `:` and `-`, optionally whitespace and characters other than `<` and `>`, an optional `/`, and `>`; once per line (C2-I-073, C2-I-124, C2-B-116)

messages: Bidi override/isolate control U+${code} is preserved by canonical Carve but not written to the text and code of presentation output; remove it unless intentional.
rules.reports: each bidirectional override or isolate control, U+202A to U+202E and U+2066 to U+2069, in text and code, the only places a render drops it: the value of a text, code span, code block or math node, title and label text included only when written between tags; a title written in an attribute, including a code title, is excluded; one finding per code point; the marks U+200E, U+200F and U+061C are not reported (C2-H-172)
rules.hand_written: C2-N-086 also runs it on the payload of a code include, with ranges in the included file, and the line model has records only for the source being linted

messages: This label holds only spaces, tabs or a line break, so it is no label and "${text}" stays text; 0.1 read it as a label. Give the label a character that is not whitespace.
rules.reports: a footnote or link reference or definition whose label is empty after folding, which is text in 0.2 and was a label in 0.1 (C2-I-079, U-340)

messages: This line begins like ${what} but parsed as plain text - the block did not open. Check this line's syntax and any unterminated fence above it.
rules.change: also a brace line that is not a valid one-line attribute line
rules.reports: a paragraph whose first text, after leading spaces and tabs, starts with a run of three or more colons, a run of three or more tildes (a refused code fence candidate under C2-B-108), or with `{.` or `{#`, a div opener or an attribute line that did not open, as `:::note` with the name glued to the run (C2-B-119), once per paragraph on its first line; and, by the row's change, a paragraph line that, after leading spaces and tabs, starts with `{` followed by `.`, `#`, `_` or an ASCII letter and is no valid attribute line, as `{a=}` (C2-B-090), once per line; a colon line that `fence-title-syntax` reports and a line that a list-indent rule reports are left to those rules (C2-B-108, C2-B-119, C2-B-090)

messages: This ${kind} is indented ${past} ${columns} past the content column of ${owner}, and it still opens a ${kind}, measured from its own line. Remove the indentation to make the structure explicit, or escape the opener to keep the line as text.
message_notes: `${columns}` is `column` when `${past}` is 1 and `columns` otherwise.
rules.range: the whole opening mark as written, without indentation or following content: the full run of `#` or `=` of a heading, of colons of a colon fence, a line block included, and of backticks or tildes of a code fence; the thematic break without trailing spaces and tabs; the quote mark; the term mark; the first `|` of a table row
rules.reports: a block opener that stands past the content column of its owner and still opens there: a quote mark, a colon fence, a code fence or line block, a definition term, a heading, a thematic break or a pipe table row, where the owner is the document (content column 0), a quote, a footnote body, a description or a div; not a list marker, not a `%%%` comment fence, not a table row directly below a row, and never inside a list item, which `list-item-block-overindented` reports; once per opener (C2-B-003, C2-B-025, C2-B-028)

messages: This line looks like ${opener} but directly follows text, so it is part of the paragraph or caption above it. Add a blank line before it.
message_notes: `${opener}` is `a heading` for a heading, `a quote` for a quote line, `an attribute line` for an attribute line, `a term` for a term mark, `a description` for a description mark and `a definition` for a definition, including an abbreviation definition (C2-B-084).
rules.reports: each line inside a paragraph or a caption that would open a block after a blank line: a heading, a quote line, an attribute line, a term or description mark, or a definition; once per candidate line, the range is the marker or attribute block on that line (C2-B-019, C2-B-200); a line that no open container owns is a lazy line of the paragraph and its candidate is its first marker, a quote mark included (C2-B-024, C2-B-025); a blank line is one as C2-W-143 reads it
rules.change: a table row and a thematic break are no triggers, because they interrupt (C2-B-019, C2-B-200)

messages.when: the line is paragraph, heading, cell, term, caption or line-block text outside frontmatter
messages.text: A blockquote marker must be bare `>` or followed by a space. This line is literal text; write `> ${text}` to quote it.

messages.when: the line is inside frontmatter
messages.text: This line is frontmatter content, not a blockquote. Close frontmatter before a quote and write `> ${text}`.

rules.range: the line from its `>` to its last character that is not a space or a tab, for both messages
rules.reports: a line of paragraph, heading, cell, term, caption or line of a line block text, or expressly a frontmatter line, whose first character, at column 1 with no indent and no container prefix before it, is `>` followed by a character that is not a space, so `>a`, `>>a` and `>` followed by a tab, which are text; a bare `>` is not reported; once per line (C2-B-031)

messages: This braced comment is a template tag. Liquid, Nunjucks, or Twig source may have reached Carve as text; the tag is parsed as an invisible comment.
rules.reports: a braced comment whose content, trimmed, is exactly `raw`, `endraw`, `endif`, `endfor` or `endblock`, or is `if`, `for` or `block` followed by whitespace and at least one further character, as `{% if x %}`; once per comment (C2-I-025)

messages: This braced span did not open: the delimiter inside it closed a span that started before it. Escape that delimiter.
rules.reports: a braced opener (C2-I-055) inside a bare emphasis or strong span that is removed and left as text because a bare delimiter after it closed that span, which opened before it (C2-I-059, C2-I-060), where a braced closer of the opener's mark follows later in the same content, so the braced span would have formed without that delimiter; a braced opener removed by a braced closer of an outer braced span, as in `{+a {*b+} c*}`, and one that has no closer of its mark are not reported; once per opener, the range is the two characters of the opener (C2-I-055, C2-I-059, C2-I-060)
rules.hand_written: it reports an opener by why the inline parse removed it (a bare delimiter closed an earlier span) and whether it would have formed otherwise; the tree and the line model keep only the result of the pairing

messages.when: the target id exists exactly but belongs to a node that is not a heading or numbered caption
messages.text: Cross-reference </#${target}> names the id "${id}", which is on a ${kind}; a cross-reference reaches only headings and numbered captions, so it renders as the literal text "</#${target}>". Link to it with [text](#${id}).

messages.when: no qualifying id matches exactly, but one or more qualifying ids differ only in case
messages.text: Cross-reference </#${target}> matches no id; ${caseOnlyPhrase}, and cross-references are case-sensitive, so it renders as the literal text "</#${target}>".

messages.when: no qualifying id matches exactly or only by case, and no exact id belongs to a nonqualifying node
messages.text: Cross-reference </#${target}> has no matching heading id; it renders as the literal text "</#${target}>".

message_notes: For case-only candidates, compare NFC-normalized keys by Unicode case folding without changing the source spelling. Order qualifying candidates by the start of their source range, then by their id spelling as Unicode code points; select the first for a singular placeholder.

`${caseOnlyPhrase}` is `the id X differs only in case` for one candidate, `the ids X and Y differ only in case` for two, and `the ids X, Y, and Z differ only in case` for three; for more candidates extend the comma-separated list in source order with `and` before the last. For reference labels, use `label` or `labels` in place of `id` or `ids`. `${caseOnly}` is the source spelling of the first qualifying rendered id.
rules.reports: a cross-reference whose id, normalized to NFC, matches no heading id, authored or generated, and no id of a table, a figure or a figure group whose caption has a number mark, nor of a panel of such a group; matching is exact, so an id that differs only in case is reported; once per cross-reference, in footnote bodies too (C2-I-096, C2-I-097, C2-B-207, C2-H-022)

messages.when: a rendered id differs only in case from the fragment as written or percent-decoded
messages.text: Link to "${href}" matches no id; the id "${caseOnly}" differs only in case, and fragment links are case-sensitive, so the link goes nowhere.

messages.when: no rendered id differs only in case from either the fragment as written or percent-decoded
messages.text: Link to "${href}" matches no id in this document, so the link goes nowhere.

message_notes: For case-only candidates, compare NFC-normalized keys by Unicode case folding without changing the source spelling. Order qualifying candidates by the start of their source range, then by their id spelling as Unicode code points; select the first for a singular placeholder.

`${caseOnlyPhrase}` is `the id X differs only in case` for one candidate, `the ids X and Y differ only in case` for two, and `the ids X, Y, and Z differ only in case` for three; for more candidates extend the comma-separated list in source order with `and` before the last. For reference labels, use `label` or `labels` in place of `id` or `ids`. `${caseOnly}` is the source spelling of the first qualifying rendered id.

For case-only comparison, test both the source fragment and its percent-decoded spelling. `${caseOnly}` names the first qualifying rendered id in source order; if both spellings find candidates, use the same order across their union.
rules.reports: a link whose destination starts with `#` and whose fragment, the part before any `:~:` and tested both as written and percent-decoded, is not empty, is not `top` in any letter case, and is no `id` (and no `name` of an `a` element) in the rendered HTML of the document under the `headingIds` of the run (C2-T-042), heading, footnote, note mark and raw HTML ids included; once per link; not reported at all while an extension that generates ids (C2-X-079) is registered for the run, whether or not the document contains a node of that extension; an extension that generates no ids changes nothing (C2-I-066, C2-H-022, C2-H-088, C2-H-089, C2-X-079)

messages.when: a pipe table starts one or two lines below this paragraph line
messages.text: This caption-looking paragraph is above the table. Move it directly below the table and start it with `^ ` to make a caption.

messages.when: no pipe table starts one or two lines below, and a pipe table row or an image marker `![` occurs in one of the two lines above
messages.text: This caption-looking paragraph sits next to a table or image-looking marker; use a ^ caption line.

rules.reports: a paragraph line whose text, after container prefixes and indent, matches case-insensitively `^(?:\*?\s*(?:Caption|Table|Tabelle|Figure|Image)(?:\s+\d+)?\s*:|:\s+\S)`; the optional number needs whitespace before its digits, so `Caption 2:` matches and `Caption2:` does not; a match reports when a pipe table row starts one or two lines above or below it or one of the two lines above holds `![`; once per line, the range is the first character of the matched line (C2-B-146, C2-B-149)

messages.when: every finding of this code
messages.text: Dropped the authored attribute ${key}: the name is reserved for roundtrip import

rules.reports: an authored attribute with a reserved carrier name (C2-H-116)

messages.when: the selected declaration has a value that is not dot-separated decimal digits
messages.text: The declared Carve version "${version}" is not a dotted numeric version. Write `0.2` as the value of this declaration, or remove it.

messages.when: the selected declaration has a dotted numeric version greater than 0.2
messages.text: This engine implements 0.2; features of the declared ${version} version may be unsupported. Write `carve: 0.2` only if the source uses 0.2 features.

message_notes: A quote or a backslash in `${version}` of the second message is escaped as in a JSON string.
rules.change: it reads the line-1 frontmatter key `carve-version` of 0.1 and the key `carve`; later blocks do not declare the document version
rules.reports: a line `carve-version:` (and, by the row's change, `carve:`) in the line-1 frontmatter block, with only spaces and tabs around the key and a single value token, whose value is not dot-separated decimal digits, or is such a version greater than 0.2 compared part by part as numbers with missing parts as 0, so `9.9`, `0.2.1` and `next` are reported and `0.1`, `0.2` and `0.2.0` are not; with no such line in the line-1 block, the same test on the `carve-version:` value of a `%%` stamp comment that ends the document; if more than one declaration meets this test, the first in source order supplies the report, `${version}` and the message condition; the range is that declaration's value token; once per document means one finding, not a document-wide range (C2-B-161, C2-B-231)

messages: The spaces at the ends of this span read otherwise than in 0.1, which removed one space from each end when both ends held one; 0.2 removes only a space next to a backtick. Check the spaces at the ends of the span.
rules.reports: a code span, a literal-text span, a math span or a raw inline span whose value differs from the value 0.1 read: 0.1 removed one space from each end when the content started and ended with a space and held a character that is not a space, and 0.2 removes only a space between a backtick and the run (C2-I-016). Since the content never starts or ends with a backtick, the 0.2 value decides it: exactly one end of the value is a backtick, or the value starts and ends with a space and holds a character that is not a space. Once per span, the range is the span
rules.change: added with the code span padding ruling of 24 November (#6525)

messages.when: the bare run is shorter than the innermost opener and long enough for no open div
messages.text: Bare ${authoredWidth}-colon fence does not close the innermost ${expectedWidth}-colon ${kind} opened at ${line}:${column}; it opens an anonymous div.

messages.when: the bare run is shorter than the innermost opener and long enough for an enclosing open container
messages.text: Bare ${authoredWidth}-colon fence does not close the innermost ${expectedWidth}-colon ${kind} opened at ${line}:${column}; it closes an enclosing container and every container inside it.

messages.when: the bare run is longer than the innermost opener
messages.text: Bare ${authoredWidth}-colon fence has a different width from the innermost ${expectedWidth}-colon ${kind} opened at ${line}:${column}; it closes the container.

message_notes: `${kind}` names the innermost open colon container: `div`, `admonition`, `figure group`, `line block` or `hard-break block` (C2-B-119, C2-B-125).
rules.range: the colon run, without indentation and without the spaces and tabs after it
rules.reports: a bare colon run, three or more colons and nothing after them but spaces and tabs, inside an open colon container (a div of any name, a line block or a hard-break block) whose innermost opener run has another length; the container counts only where it is open inside the run's own innermost container, so a run in a quote or list item that sits in a div, with no colon container open inside that quote or item, is not reported, since it cannot close the outer div (C2-B-109); the run closes the innermost open container it is long enough for and every one inside it, or opens an anonymous div when it is long enough for none, and the message names that outcome; once per run (C2-B-108, C2-B-109, C2-B-125)

messages: This line starts with a percent run and holds other text, so it is content of the comment block and does not close it. Put the closing run alone on its line.
rules.reports: a line inside a comment block that starts with a `%` run of at least the opener's length and holds other text: it is content in 0.2 and closed the block in 0.1 (C2-B-110, C2-B-195)

messages: A line comment starts inside this reference label and takes the rest of the line, so the brackets are text. Move the comment out of the label, or escape the percent signs.
rules.reports: a line comment that starts inside a reference label and takes the rest of the line, so that the brackets are text (C2-I-077)
rules.hand_written: whether the brackets would form a reference label is a parse of the line without the comment, and no record gives a construct the comment kept from forming

messages: A line comment is text inside a line block. Use the braced comment.
rules.reports: a line of a line block that starts with `%%` and opens no comment block (C2-B-123)

messages: This span looks like a C comment; use Carve comment syntax if you meant a comment.
rules.reports: an emphasis span whose source starts with `/*` or ends with `*/`, or a strong span whose source starts with `*/` or ends with `/*`, as `/* foo */`; braced forms are not reported; once per span, at hint severity (C2-I-046, C2-I-052)

messages: This comment stands between a table row and its continuation, so it belongs after the whole row. Move it above the row or below the continuation.
rules.reports: a comment-only line, or the trailing comment of a row, between a table row and its continuation row (C2-A-086, C2-B-175)

messages: "${word}" is not a consumed key here; did you mean {${key}}?
rules.change: `loose` leaves the list of consumed keys
rules.reports: a bare key with an empty value in the attributes of a `csv` or `tsv` code block, captioned or not, that is not `table` but is `table` in another letter case or one edit from it (an inserted, deleted or replaced character, or two adjacent characters swapped), as `tabel`, `tables`, `Table` or `atble`; once per key; `loose` on a list is no longer a consumed key (C2-B-180, C2-B-227, C2-B-066)

messages.when: the line continues a link definition or an abbreviation definition
messages.text: This indented line continues the definition above in 0.2; in 0.1 it started a paragraph. Remove the indent to make it a separate block again.

messages.when: the line continues a term
messages.text: This indented line continues the term above in 0.2; in 0.1 it started a paragraph. Remove the indent to make it a separate block again.

messages.when: the line stands directly below a caption and is not indented past its caret
messages.text: This line ends the caption above in 0.2; in 0.1 it continued the caption. Indent it past the caret to keep it in the caption.

rules.reports: a line whose reading changed between 0.1 and 0.2, where 0.2 reads it as C2-B-083, C2-B-084 and C2-B-234 say: the first line below the first line of a link definition or an abbreviation definition that the definition takes, a tail line or an expansion line, which 0.1 read as a paragraph (C2-B-083, C2-B-084), once per definition; the first line below the mark line of a term, comment-only lines skipped, that continues the term, which is indented past the term mark and which 0.1 read as a paragraph (C2-B-069, C2-B-234), once per term; and the line directly below the last line of a caption that the caption does not take, because it is not indented past the caret, when it carries as many quote marks as that last line and is text, a block image line, a display math line, a list item marker line, a description line or a heading line that starts with `=`, which 0.1 read as a lazy line of the caption (C2-B-148, C2-B-234); the range is that line
rules.change: added with the continuation rulings of 24 November (#6507, #6508)

messages: A definition is recognized only at column 0 outside every container, so this line is text. Put it at column 0 outside every container.
rules.reports: each definition-shaped line inside a container or indented at the top level; once per candidate line, the range is the bracketed label and colon, or the snippet marker and colon (C2-B-081, C2-B-236)

messages: A quote mark or list marker after the term mark is term text. Put the intended block on a `: ` description line at the list column, such as `: > text` or `: - item`.
rules.change: a block opener under a term is term text (C2-B-075)
rules.reports: a term whose text (C2-B-069) starts with a quote mark (C2-B-031) or a list marker (C2-B-034, C2-B-036) followed by a space, which C2-B-075 makes term text; `:: >a` and a block opener on a later line of the term are not reported; once per term, the range is the quote mark or the list marker (C2-B-031, C2-B-034, C2-B-036, C2-B-069, C2-B-075)

messages: This marked CSV/TSV fence has malformed quoting. It stays a table, and the cell with the unclosed quote holds the rest of the fence body.
rules.channel_reports: an unclosed quote in a delimited table (C2-B-181)
rules.change: severity error; new message text: the block stays a table (C2-B-181)
rules.reports: an unclosed quote in a delimited table: a `"` at the start of a field of a `csv` or `tsv` fence marked with `table` that finds no closing `"` before the end of the fence body, so its cell holds the rest of the body (C2-B-181); a `"` inside an unquoted field and text after a closing quote are no bad quoting in 0.2 and are not reported; once per table, the range is the unclosed quote character (C2-B-180, C2-B-181)

messages: A CSV/TSV record has more fields than the first record; the table keeps the extra columns.
rules.reports: a delimited table, a `csv` or `tsv` fence that the `table` attribute marks, in which any record has more fields than the first record; once per table (C2-B-180, C2-B-226)

messages: A bare equals pair is text in 0.2. Write the braced highlight.
rules.reports: a pair of bare `=` in one inline content that 0.1 read as highlight, read as if `=` were a bare delimiter of C2-I-046: the opener can open by C2-I-047, stands next to no other `=`, is not followed by `>` and is not the `=` of `!=`, `<=` or `>=` (C2-I-117); the closer is the first later `=` that can close by C2-I-048 and is not the `=` of such a comparison, and a `=` between them that cannot close is text, so the pair does not nest; the content between them is not empty and may hold line breaks and other spans, and no pair forms where that content holds `=` between two word characters (C2-I-053); a bare `=` followed by a combining mark, a variation selector or a zero-width joiner (C2-I-050) takes no part; once per pair, the range runs from the opener to the end of the closer (C2-I-046, C2-I-047, C2-I-048, C2-I-050, C2-I-053, C2-I-117)

messages: A bare tilde pair is text in 0.2. Write the braced strike.
rules.reports: a pair of bare `~` in one inline content that 0.1 read as strike, read as if `~` were a bare delimiter of C2-I-046: the opener can open by C2-I-047, stands next to no other `~`; the closer is the first later `~` that can close by C2-I-048, and a `~` between them that cannot close is text, so the pair does not nest; the content between them is not empty and may hold line breaks and other spans, and no pair forms where that content holds `~` between two word characters (C2-I-053); a bare `~` followed by a combining mark, a variation selector or a zero-width joiner (C2-I-050) takes no part; once per pair, the range runs from the opener to the end of the closer (C2-I-046, C2-I-047, C2-I-048, C2-I-050, C2-I-053)

messages: A bare underscore pair is text in 0.2. Write the braced underline, or the slash pair for emphasis.
rules.reports: a pair of bare `_` in one inline content that 0.1 read as underline, read as if `_` were a bare delimiter of C2-I-046: the opener can open by C2-I-047, stands next to no other `_`; the closer is the first later `_` that can close by C2-I-048, and a `_` between them that cannot close is text, so the pair does not nest; the content between them is not empty and may hold line breaks and other spans, and no pair forms where that content holds `_` between two word characters (C2-I-053); a bare `_` followed by a combining mark, a variation selector or a zero-width joiner (C2-I-050) takes no part; once per pair, the range runs from the opener to the end of the closer (C2-I-046, C2-I-047, C2-I-048, C2-I-050, C2-I-053)

messages: The table cell alignment prefix "${prefix}" is the deprecated 0.1.13 spelling, removed in 0.2.0. Alignment symbols now lead the cell's attribute block: write "${braced}". In 0.2 the old prefix is cell text, so the formatter leaves it; the upgrade tool rewrites it.
rules.change: the glued alignment marker is cut; the rule stays on through 0.2.x
rules.reports: a cell of a complete pipe table row, whose text starts directly after the pipe, behind the header mark `=` if any, with a valid 0.1.13 alignment run (a horizontal `<`, `>` or `~` with an optional vertical `^`, `~` or `v`, or `?` with a vertical mark), optionally a glued brace block, then a space; a cell that holds only `<` or `^` and a cell that starts with a brace block are not reported; once per cell (C2-B-171, C2-B-182)

messages.when: the `+` is a standalone line outside a list item
messages.text: The plus continuation marker was removed in 0.2 and is text here. If a block was intended, write that block after a blank line.

messages.when: the `+` is a standalone line inside a list item but not its marker line
messages.text: The plus continuation marker was removed in 0.2 and is text inside this list item. Put the intended block after a blank line, indented past the list marker so it belongs to this item.

messages.when: the `+` is the text of a list item marker line
messages.text: The plus continuation marker was removed in 0.2 and is text here. Put the intended block after a blank line, indented past the list marker so it belongs to this item.

rules.reports: a line whose content behind its quote marks and indentation is a single `+`, with only spaces and tabs before and after it, and a list item, with or without a task box, whose text on its marker line is a single `+`, both text in 0.2 where 0.1 read a list continuation marker (C2-B-059); `++`, `+a` and a table cell holding `+` are not reported; once per line, the range is the `+` (C2-B-059)

messages: This indented line directly below a heading is part of the heading in 0.2; in 0.1 it started a paragraph. Remove the indent to make it a separate block again; if it then reads as a list marker or another opener and a paragraph is meant, escape its first character.
rules.reports: a line directly below a heading line, or below it across comment-only lines, that is indented past the heading marker and so continues the heading
rules.change: added with the heading continuation rule

messages: The loose attribute was removed in 0.2 and is a plain attribute here. A list is loose when a blank line stands between two of its items.
rules.reports: a list that carries the key `loose`

messages: The separator row was removed in 0.2 and is a row of dashes here. Mark the header cells with the header mark and delete this row.
rules.reports: the second row of a table whose first row is not such a row, when every cell of it holds, inside its padding, only a run of one or more hyphens with an optional colon at either end (`-`, `---`, `:--`, `--:`, `:-:`) and has no cell prefix: the separator row 0.1 read as the end of a Markdown head, which 0.2 reads as an ordinary body row (C2-B-166); a row of hyphens at any other place, a lone first row, an empty cell and a cell with a header mark or a brace block are not reported; once per row, the range is the row (C2-B-166, C2-B-171)

messages: A spaced thematic break was removed in 0.2; this line is a list item (or text). Write the unspaced star form.
rules.reports: a line that after its container prefixes and indent holds only three or more stars, hyphens or underscores with spaces between them, the container prefixes being quote marks and the markers of items, descriptions and footnote bodies up to their content column (C2-B-027); markers that the run itself makes, as `- - -` reads as nested items (C2-B-058), belong to the run and not to the prefixes, so `- - -` and `a. - - -` both report the whole spaced run; the range is the run
rules.change: unchanged; `- - -` is this case

messages: The substitution arrow was removed in 0.2; this is a strike span. Write a deletion directly followed by an insertion.
rules.reports: a braced strike span whose own content holds `~>`, which 0.1 read as a substitution of the text before by the text after and which 0.2 reads as text in the strike (C2-I-062): the first `~>` not behind a backslash in the strike's own inline content, outside a nested braced span or bracket construct, while a bare span around it does not hide it; once per strike span, the range is the strike span (C2-I-062)

messages.when: a tab separates a parsed code-fence language from later info-string parts
messages.text: The tab does not separate valid info-string parts; the block keeps its language, but does not keep the later title or label. Use "${respaced}" with spaces between parts.

message_notes: `${label}` is a space followed by the bracketed label when one is present, and the empty string otherwise.
`${correctedOpener}` keeps the fence run and any valid type, title and label before the further words, omitting the further words; attributes go on their own line above it.
`${respaced}` has one space after the fence run and between valid info-string parts, with no tab; where no info-string part is valid it is the fence run alone.

`${fence}` is the authored fence run; `${type}` is the parsed code-fence language; `${title}` is the authored title text without its surrounding quotes when quoted, otherwise the later text proposed as a title. These values come from the reported opener; if a value is absent, substitute the empty string.

rules.reports: a table cell that holds only a span mark, `<` or `^`, after any prefix, that joins nothing and so holds the mark as text: a `<` in the first column or whose left cell is covered by a row span from above, a `^` in the first row of its group (head, body or foot) or below a cell that spans more than one column; once per cell, an escaped mark is not reported, and the range is the cell, the text between its pipes (C2-B-172, C2-B-173, C2-B-174)

messages: The specified table column widths total more than 100%.
rules.reports: a table whose `widths` attribute has a valid whole list under C2-B-212 and whose entries total more than 100; an invalid list reports only `table-attribute-invalid`; once per table, the range is the key `widths` (C2-B-212)

messages: This line of "${raw}" is text in Carve 0.2. Write "***" for a thematic break.
rules.change: new trigger: a run of hyphens or underscores alone on a line, which is text in 0.2
rules.reports: a line of text that after its container prefixes and indent holds only a run of three or more hyphens or of three or more underscores and trailing spaces and tabs, which is no thematic break in 0.2, once per line; a hyphen run directly below a line of paragraph text is reported by `setext-heading-underline` instead, and three hyphens on line 1 open frontmatter; a typed opener that forms a later block is not text; the range is the run (C2-B-160, C2-B-161, C2-B-232)

messages: A blank line inside an item no longer makes the list loose. Put a blank line between the items if every item should render as a paragraph.
rules.reports: a tight list (C2-B-062) in which an item holds a paragraph among its own blocks and a blank line between two of its own blocks, which 0.1 read as a loose list and which 0.2 keeps tight, so the first paragraph of each item is written bare (C2-H-034); a blank line inside a nested block does not count; once per list, the range is the list (C2-B-062, C2-H-034)

messages.when: the attribute line reaches the end of its container or document without a following blank line
messages.text: This attribute line reaches no block: a blank line or the end of its container follows, so the line is text (C2-B-192). Move it directly above the block it describes, or delete it.

messages.when: a blank line follows the attribute line in its container, whether or not a block follows that blank line
messages.text: A blank line follows this attribute line, so it is text. Remove the blank line if you mean to attach it to a following block.

rules.change: also an attribute line separated from its block by a blank line, which is text
rules.reports: an attribute line, or a run of consecutive attribute lines reported once at its first line, that no block takes because the end of its container or of the document follows, and since 0.2 also one that a blank line follows, a line blank as C2-W-143 reads it; a line the parse reads as text of a paragraph is no attribute line (C2-W-107), and `block-opener-without-blank-line` reports it; once per run, the range is the attribute line (C2-B-090, C2-B-092, C2-B-192, C2-W-143)

messages: This caption line is not directly below an image, table, code block, quote, math block, figure group or code include, so it is text. If a blank line separates it from such a block, remove the blank line; otherwise escape the caret.
rules.reports: a caption line that is not directly below an image, table, code block, quote, math block, figure group or valid code include, a caption after a blank line among them, and a caption line directly below a caption that the same container holds (C2-B-149)
rules.change: the target list has seven kinds, the figure group and code include included

messages: This attribute block is attached to nothing and renders as text. Glue it to a span, link or code span, or escape the brace.
rules.reports: a valid attribute block, or a run of glued ones, in an inline content (a paragraph, heading, term, description or table cell) that is glued to the end of no formed host (C2-I-036), so it is printed as written (C2-I-035); a line of a line block is such an inline content too, and the text of a caption or a description is that of its paragraphs; `{}`, an escaped brace, a line that holds nothing but blocks (an attribute line), a run at the start of a paragraph or of a line of a line block that `block-marker-as-text` reports and a table cell that `table-row-attribute-as-cell` reports are not reported; once per run, the range is the run (C2-I-028, C2-I-035, C2-I-036)

messages: This braced comment is not closed before the next block starts, so it stays text. Close it inside its block, or use %% line comments.
rules.reports: a braced comment whose closer stands behind an interrupter line, so that it is unclosed and stays text (C2-B-141)

messages: The ${marker} fence opened here has no closing fence; ${ending}. Add a closing ${marker} where the code should stop.
message_notes: `${ending}` is "it runs to the end of the document" or "it ends at the end of its container on line ${line}".
rules.channel_reports: a code fence that runs to the end of its container (C2-B-111)
rules.change: severity error; the block ends with its container (C2-B-111)
rules.reports: a code fence, a raw fence included, that has no closing fence before its container ends, so it ends with its container or with the document, once per fence; the range is the block (C2-B-111)

messages.when: every finding of this code
messages.text: The ${opener} comment fence opened here has no closing fence and hides everything to the end of its container (or: the document). Add a closing ${opener} where the comment should stop.

rules.channel_reports: a comment block that runs to the end of its container (C2-B-111)
rules.change: severity error; the block ends with its container (C2-B-111)
rules.reports: a comment block, opened by a run of three or more percent signs, that has no closing run before its container ends, so it ends with its container or with the document, once per block; the range is the block (C2-B-111)

messages.when: the unclosed container is a named div, admonition, directive, figure group, quote fence or line block
messages.text: This ${width}-colon ${kind} has no closer; it runs to the end of its container. Add a bare fence of ${width} colons to close it.

messages.when: the unclosed container is an anonymous div
messages.text: This ${width}-colon container has no closer; add a bare fence of ${width} colons to close it.

rules.channel_reports: a div that runs to the end of its container (C2-B-111, C2-B-125)
rules.change: severity error; the block ends with its container (C2-B-111)
rules.reports: a div of any kind, plain, anonymous, admonition, directive, figure group, quote fence or line block, whose colon run meets no bare colon run long enough to close it before its container ends, once per div; a stray colon run at column 0 below an item with an unclosed div opens an anonymous div at top level, which is reported too; the range is the div (C2-B-111, C2-B-125, C2-B-132)

messages: This frontmatter block has no closing line, so it runs to the end of the document.
rules.reports: frontmatter with no closer
rules.change: unchanged (C2-B-163)

messages: This ${span} opener is unclosed in its paragraph; add a closer.
message_notes: `${span}` is `strong` for `*` and `emphasis` for `/`.
rules.reports: a bare `*` or `/` in a paragraph line that stands at the start of the line or after whitespace, `(`, `[` or `{`, that an ASCII letter, digit or `_` follows, that closes no pair, and after which the rest of its paragraph holds no further delimiter of its kind; once per delimiter (C2-I-046, C2-I-047, C2-I-051)

messages: This marker stands left of every open list and continues the list above it. Align it with the markers of that list.
rules.reports: a marker left of every open list that continues the list above it, except an ordered marker that `ordered-marker-right-aligned` reports (C2-B-054, C2-B-030)

messages: Footnote reference [^${id}] has no matching definition; it renders as literal text.
rules.reports: a footnote reference that resolves to no footnote definition, its key folded as C2-I-079 says and its case kept; once per reference (C2-I-087, C2-I-088, C2-I-079)

messages.when: the unresolved reference is a link and a label or heading differs from its key only in case
messages.text: Reference link ${rawRef} matches no link definition or heading; ${caseOnlyPhrase}, and reference labels are case-sensitive, so its brackets and label remain literal, while link-text children render normally.

messages.when: the unresolved reference is a link with no label or heading that differs only in case
messages.text: Reference link ${rawRef} has no matching link definition or heading; its brackets and label remain literal, while link-text children render normally.

messages.when: the unresolved reference is an image and a link definition label differs from its key only in case
messages.text: Reference image ${rawRef} matches no link definition; ${caseOnlyPhrase}, and reference labels are case-sensitive, so its marker, brackets, label and alt text render as literal text.

messages.when: the unresolved reference is an image with no link definition label that differs only in case
messages.text: Reference image ${rawRef} has no matching link definition; its marker, brackets, label and alt text render as literal text.

rules.change: the full form and a wrapped label now reach the heading lookup (C2-I-080, C2-I-081)
message_notes: For case-only candidates, compare NFC-normalized keys by Unicode case folding without changing the source spelling. Order qualifying candidates by the start of their source range, then by their id spelling as Unicode code points; select the first for a singular placeholder.

`${caseOnlyPhrase}` is `the id X differs only in case` for one candidate, `the ids X and Y differ only in case` for two, and `the ids X, Y, and Z differ only in case` for three; for more candidates extend the comma-separated list in source order with `and` before the last. For reference labels, use `label` or `labels` in place of `id` or `ids`. `${caseOnly}` is the source spelling of the first qualifying rendered id.
rules.reports: a full or collapsed reference, link or image, whose key matches no link definition and, for a link, no heading by the lookup of C2-I-084, once per reference; a shortcut forms only from a definition and is text otherwise, so it is never reported, and a wrapped label folds its line break to one space; the range is the reference (C2-I-081, C2-I-080, C2-A-109)

messages: Footnote definition [^${label}] is never referenced, so it is omitted from the rendered document.
rules.reports: a footnote definition whose key no footnote reference of the document uses, a reference inside another footnote definition counting; once per key, the range is `[^label]` on the definition's first line (C2-B-082, C2-H-194)

messages: This link reference definition is unused.
rules.reports: a link reference definition whose key no link or image reference that resolves uses, where a reference inside a footnote definition that nothing references, and one inside an unresolved reference, does not count; once per definition, from its opening bracket (C2-B-083, C2-I-075, C2-H-193)

messages: Snippet "$${name}" is defined but never used.
rules.reports: a winning snippet definition that no snippet use of the authored tree names, a use inside another definition counted; once per definition, the range is the `$` and the name in its marker (C2-N-096)
rules.hand_written: it needs the snippet registry of the expanded tree and the names that its uses resolve to, which no record of the model holds

rules.reports: the writer reached a repeated repair state or its repair limit (C2-W-133)
